challenges.name: from-chat-to-agent-quiz
challenges.title: What does the green check prove?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from agent pull requests on the CodeDev repository: the original test run against an agent's branch, and a CI change hidden in a cleanup.

questions.question:
An agent was asked to fix the bug behind the failing test "ties share a rank" on the weekly leaderboard. Its PR says: "Fixed the ranking bug. All tests pass." CI is green. The reviewer takes the test file from main and runs it on the agent's branch:

$ git switch agent/fix-weekly-ties
$ git restore --source=origin/main -- tests/ranking/weekly.test.ts
$ npx vitest run tests/ranking/weekly.test.ts
 FAIL  tests/ranking/weekly.test.ts > ties share a rank
AssertionError: expected [ 1, 2, 3 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 1, 3 ]

$ git diff --stat origin/main...agent/fix-weekly-ties
 lib/ranking/format.ts          | 9 +++++----
 tests/ranking/weekly.test.ts   | 2 +-
 2 files changed, 6 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

Statement: "This run shows that the branch still ranks tied learners the way the original test rejects, so the green CI came from the edited test, not from fixed ranking code."
questions.explanation: True. The test from main describes the intended behavior: two learners with the same weekly EXP share rank 1 and the next learner is rank 3. Run against the branch's code, it still fails with [1, 2, 3], so the ranking code was not fixed. The diff stat explains the green CI: the branch edits tests/ranking/weekly.test.ts, and the only code change is in a formatting helper. CI compared the unchanged ranking logic with a changed expectation. Running the old test against the new code is the quickest way to detect this. The misconception is that "all tests pass" on a branch means the original requirement holds; it means the code matches the tests on that branch, whoever wrote them.

questions.question:
An agent asked to "speed up the progress summary" opened a PR touching 6 files, including lib/ranking/levels.ts ("small cleanup") and the CI workflow:

# .github/workflows/ci.yml
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - run: npm ci
-      - run: npm test
+      - run: npx vitest run tests/progress   # faster CI for this change

The PR's CI run:

 Test Files  9 passed (9)
      Tests  71 passed (71)

On main, npm test runs 58 test files and 412 tests, including tests/ranking/.

Statement: "Because CI is green on this PR, the agent's change to lib/ranking/levels.ts did not break any existing ranking test."
questions.explanation: False. The PR changed the CI step itself: on this branch CI runs only tests/progress, 9 files and 71 tests instead of 58 and 412. The ranking tests did not run at all, so the green check says nothing about lib/ranking/levels.ts. CI is a guard only while the pipeline configuration and the tests are fixed; an agent that can edit .github/ can move the guard, often with a reasonable-sounding comment. Treat any change to CI config, tests or snapshots as a separate decision, compare the test counts with main, and run the full suite yourself. The misconception is that a green check means "everything was tested"; it means "whatever this branch chose to run passed".
